title: U.S sprinter Jordan Anthony wins 60m indoor title on world championship debut
content:
American sprinter Jordan Anthony has won his debut world title with a 6.41 second run over 60m in Torun, Poland.

The 21-year-old, running out of lane four, was quickest out of the blocks and held that lead to beat Kishane Thompson of Jamaica, who with a 6.45s run won the silver medal.

Thompson ran just one thousandth quicker than Trayvon Bromell, the 30-year-old American, who finished third to take another global indoor 60m medal a decade after he won the world title in this event.

Anthony took down a field that included Olympic and World medallist Thompson, compatriot Bromell, and defending 60m world champion Jeremiah Azu — the Brit finished fourth in 6.46s, the fastest non-medallist time in indoor championships history.

The American’s time was the quickest in the world this year — he arrived as world No 1 with his 6.43s title-winning run from the U.S. indoor championships to beat Noah Lyles — and he now sits joint-fourth on the all-time list. Andre Carson and 2020 Olympic 100m champion Lamont Marcell Jacobs have also run 6.41s.

“This is my first time being out of the country,” Anthony told reporters after the heats Friday morning. “I feel like I’m still the underdog, because I’m a child to them. I’m here to validate myself.”

He certainly did that on his global championships debut.

This title is a significant achievement for Anthony, who calls himself a ‘young buck’ in his first year as a professional. He previously played college football as a wide receiver for the University of Kentucky and University of Arkansas, being a dual athlete as a sprinter in their track teams too.

“I was not nervous. I haven’t been nervous since I got off the plane, honestly. I just couldn’t sleep,” he said in the mixed zone, adding that he spends much of his spare time watching and studying his competitors.

“I love watching different people race, I love knowing who I’m running against, knowing the field of play, and being a student, it’s just like me playing football, I’ve got to watch him or the other team.”

“The time is fast, yes, but I’ve been competing against high-caliber talent (in the) NCAA,” he added.

“There’s no cakewalk in the semifinals, the finals, or anything.”

Last year, Anthony won NCAA division one titles over 60m and 100m, the first man to hold both in the same calendar year since Christian Coleman in 2017. In 2025 he produced a wind-assisted 9.75s run for 100m, which ranks in the top 10 all-time for performances in all conditions.

Now Anthony is the American and World Champion, having taken down his second high-calibre field in the space of a month.

The youngster navigated the rounds excellently, running 6.54s to win his heat and coming out on top in the third of three semi-finals. That pitted Anthony against Azu and Jamaica’s Ackeem Blake, and the American equalled his then-personal best to finish first and ensure a good lane draw for the final.

“God put this dog in me. I’m going to always release the dog when it’s time for me to release,” he said after the final.

He ran all three rounds with tape on his left forearm, which Anthony explained in the mixed zone was a fix for a blood clot which had occurred during regulation drug testing when he arrived in Poland.

“There’s not much I can do with it right now because it’s still very sore,” he explained, showing reporters that he was unable to fully extend his right arm. “It was not going to stop me from winning this battle, it could have fallen off and I would still be running.”

Anthony’s gold and Bromell’s bronze extends the excellent run for American men over 60m at the world indoor championships. They now have 24 medals and 11 golds in the event, with Anthony the 11th different winner.
